writeup: TIC 341290373 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 1.8748 days, detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The primary eclipse produces a 2.50% dimming signal with a detection significance of 209.9 on the BLS scale, while no secondary eclipse was detected. Pixel-level image analysis yields a difference-imaging peak signal-to-noise of 35.0, though the centroid offset of 1.7 arcsec raises an important limitation: TESS's resolution cannot confidently separate this target from a nearby bright star. The on-target determination relies on a centroid margin of only 0.029 pixels, well within the instrument's known systematic uncertainty of 0.10-0.3 pixels. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs. Confirmation through additional observations would be needed to establish whether this signal originates from the intended target or from blended starlight.
